claim: Under a Xiaohongshu thread asking which app nobody has built (761 likes, 1,130 saves, 214 comments), the most specific repeated request is not calorie counting — it is food logging read against your own medical check-up report, and commenters say the existing apps cover too little and nobody has the standing to build it.
method: Mined Xiaohongshu directly rather than a scout feed: four search terms (市面上还缺 / 求一个能的app / 为什么没人做这个app / 每次都要自己), four high-engagement notes opened, comment trees extracted verbatim. Three independent commenters in one thread converge on the same missing product, and one names the blocker. Cross-checked against the operator's own starred radar entries #1+102 and #533, which sit on the same 体检报告 line.
hook: Someone walks out of a check-up with three numbers flagged red, and by the time they are standing in the supermarket aisle holding two packets, the report is useless to them.
does: Nothing yet — this is the shape of the hole. What people are asking for: point the phone at a nutrition label, and get a verdict that knows what their own bloodwork said. Not a calorie diary; a buy / do-not-buy / swap-this call, grounded in the report they already paid for.
edge: It converts a document people already receive once a year and then file away into a decision they make forty times a week.
why_use: The report says 'triglycerides high'. The aisle says 'contains vegetable oil, maltose syrup, 12g sugar per 100g'. Nobody translates between those two, so the report changes nothing.
gap: Existing apps only count calories, but users want food logging judged against their own medical check-up report, which requires medical data integration and trust.
counter: This is health-adjacent, so the honest ceiling is low: you can translate and compare, you cannot advise, and the moment it says 'do not eat this' it is practising medicine. Chinese platforms are also circling — a big check-up chain or an insurer can bundle it, and 薄荷 can add label OCR in one release. The deeper risk is behavioural: people who read labels already read labels, and people who do not will not start because an app asked them to.
differentiator: Refuse the hospital-integration fantasy that everyone in that comment thread assumes is required. The user uploads the PDF or photo of the report they already hold, three to five flagged lines get turned into three to five plain-language shopping rules, and from then on the product does exactly one thing: photograph a nutrition label, get a one-line verdict against those rules plus one alternative on the same shelf. No diet plan, no diagnosis, no meal logging, and every verdict ends with what to ask a doctor or dietitian. Cold start (Chinese): the comment tree of this note and 「配料表 怎么看」 / 「体检报告 解读」 on Xiaohongshu, where people are already posting label photos and asking strangers; Cold start (English): r/nutrition and r/loseit, search 'which one should I buy' and 'read my bloodwork'.
value: Someone who just got a report with red lines on it — the highest-intent moment there is. One-off unlock or a yearly fee timed to the annual check-up, not a subscription to a food diary.
risk: The self-imposed ceiling (translate and compare, never advise) is also the reason it may feel too thin to pay for.
consumer_angle: An app that scans nutrition labels and tells you whether to buy/eat based on your personal bloodwork, not just calories.

voices.quote: 要输入自己吃的食物、习惯分析缺许多维生素、各类营养物质和热量的，还可以接入体检报告，fit那个功能太有限了。这种软件需要专业的医院和医生以及大量数据来做，可惜没人做。
有没有可以拍照食品营养成分表，自动文字识别录入信息，进行汇总和比对的
非ai的薄荷其实大模型应该直接可以，还有一个火了的caloris

zh.claim: 小红书一条「有没有哪种APP，真的很需要但没人做？」（761赞/1130收藏/214评论）下面，被反复提到、也最具体的那个需求不是数卡路里，而是「吃了什么 × 我自己的体检报告」；评论区自己给出了结论：现有产品覆盖不全，而且普通人「没权限做」。
zh.hook: 一个人拿着体检报告走出医院，上面飘红三项；等他站在超市货架前手里捏着两包东西时，那份报告对他毫无用处。
zh.does: 目前还什么都没有——这是那个洞的形状。人们要的是：手机对着配料表拍一下，得到一句知道自己血脂什么样的判断。不是饮食日记，是「买 / 别买 / 换这个」，依据是他已经花钱做过的那份报告。
zh.gap: 痛点击中了，而现有产品全都在解另一半。薄荷 / Cal AI / Caloris 是卡路里日记——你记的是已经吃下去的。没人在你掏钱之前读那张包装背面，也没人把任何一头接到体检报告上。评论区自己说出了拦路虎：他们默认这事要接医院数据——而正是这个默认，让根本不需要医院数据的「货架那一侧」至今空着。
zh.counter: 这是贴着健康的东西，诚实的天花板就很低：你只能翻译和比对，不能建议；一旦它说出「这个别吃」，那就是行医。国内平台也在边上转——某家体检连锁或保险公司可以直接打包送，薄荷加一个配料表识别也就是一个版本的事。更深的风险在行为上：会看配料表的人本来就在看，不看的人不会因为一个 App 就开始看。
zh.differentiator: 拒绝评论区所有人都默认必须有的那个「接医院」幻想。用户上传自己手里已经有的那份报告（PDF 或拍照），把飘红的三到五项变成三到五条买东西时的规则；此后产品只干一件事：拍配料表，出一句对照这几条规则的判断，外加同一层货架上的一个替代品。不做食谱、不做诊断、不做饮食记录，每一句判断后面都跟一句「该去问医生/营养师什么」。冷启动（中文）：这条笔记的评论树，以及小红书「配料表 怎么看」「体检报告 解读」——人们已经在那里贴包装照片问陌生人了；冷启动（英文）：r/nutrition 与 r/loseit 搜 which one should I buy、read my bloodwork。
zh.value: 刚拿到飘红报告的那个人——意图最强的一刻。一次性解锁或按年，跟着年度体检走，不做饮食日记的月订阅。
zh.risk: 那条自己划下的天花板（只翻译只比对、绝不建议），同时也是它可能薄到没人愿意付钱的原因。
zh.why_use: 报告写「甘油三酯偏高」，货架写「植物油、麦芽糖浆、每100克含糖12克」。没人在这两句话之间做翻译，于是报告什么也没改变。
zh.edge: 把一份一年领一次、领完就归档的文件，变成一周要做四十次的决定。

pick_reason: Pain is verified by specific comments, but the wedge is unclear due to medical data access and trust barriers.
